title: Spawned campaign ensembles and convergence certificates
summary: Runs independent cases through safe spawned local processes, fingerprints declared and resolved scientific inputs, and issues conservative multi-axis convergence certificates.

science.statement: A scalable refinement study remains scientific evidence only when execution resources, failed cases, fixed coordinates, observable policies, and input identity coverage remain explicit.

equations.label: finest relative change
equations.description: The metric is evaluated per declared observable on an explicit coarse-to-fine slice.

equations.label: uniform-ratio observed order
equations.description: Order is reported only for at least three samples with matching successive refinement ratios.

inputs.name: campaign cases
inputs.description: Each independent case has a deterministic identity and fresh construction boundary.

inputs.name: refinement axes
inputs.type: positive characteristic size or inverse resolution with fixed coordinates
inputs.description: Prevents unrelated parameter changes from entering a convergence sequence.

inputs.name: scientific inputs
inputs.type: files, arrays, mappings, or objects with IR/summary contracts
inputs.unit_role: preserved by the public scientific record
inputs.description: Opaque objects remain explicit coverage gaps.

outputs.name: CampaignReport
outputs.type: ordered case records, worker evidence, runtime and input manifests
outputs.description: Failed cases remain addressable and completed cases are resumable.

outputs.name: ConvergenceCertificate
outputs.type: passed, failed, or inconclusive checks per axis and observable
outputs.unit_role: relative metrics are dimensionless; absolute metrics inherit output units
outputs.description: Includes case IDs, characteristic sizes, values, criteria, and a stable certificate identity.

assumptions: Each local worker can import and serialize the Campaign build/evaluate callables.
Each case constructs fresh mutable solver state.
Convergence axes are positive and all other varying parameters are explicitly fixed.
Exact event/topology records are JSON-safe scientific evidence.
conventions: Across-case local execution uses spawn and cannot be nested inside within-case MPI.
Characteristic sizes are ordered coarse-to-fine; inverse resolution converts element counts to decreasing size.
Missing or failed refinement cases make a check inconclusive.
applicability: Local workstation parameter sweeps, mesh/time/cohesive resolution studies, event-order stability, topology checks, and evidence generation before learning or publication.
limitations: No scheduler or independently launched MPI-job ensemble provider is included yet.
The initial certificate does not calculate generalized GCI or uncertainty intervals.
Field comparison uses declared numeric arrays; mesh-transfer norms require a future field policy.
Complete input identity depends on explicit files or public IR/summary contracts.

usage.minimal_example: campaign = campaigns.create(..., execution=campaigns.local_processes(workers=4), scientific_inputs={"mesh": Path("mesh.inp")}); report = campaign.run(plan); certificate = convergence.audit(report, axes=(convergence.axis("h", fixed={"dt": 1e-3}),), observables=(convergence.observable("response", tolerance=0.01),))

validation_rules: Reject local-process nesting inside a within-case MPI communicator.
Reject duplicate axis or observable declarations.
Report failed, missing, duplicate-size, or insufficient refinement sequences as inconclusive.
Mark objects without scientific identity contracts as incomplete coverage.

references.title: Python multiprocessing contexts and start methods
